variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Discriminative models learn the relationship needed to predict a target from an input. Generative models learn how data is distributed, often jointly with a target or through latent variables, so they can score, reconstruct, complete, or create observations.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Discriminative
pairs.detail: Estimate P(y | x) or a direct score f(x).
pairs.explanation: Estimate P(y | x) or a direct score f(x). Logistic regression, support vector machines, conditional random fields, and many classifiers follow this pattern.

pairs.label: Generative
pairs.detail: Estimate P(x, y), P(x | y), or a latent-variable distribution.
pairs.explanation: Estimate P(x, y), P(x | y), or a latent-variable distribution. Naive Bayes, hidden Markov models, variational autoencoders, diffusion models, and autoregressive models are examples.

variants.hint:
Discriminative: Estimate P(y | x) or a direct score f(x).

Generative: Estimate P(x, y), P(x | y), or a latent-variable distribution.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Reject
pairs.detail: Return no prediction when required evidence is absent.
pairs.explanation: Return no prediction when required evidence is absent. Availability moves to a retry, fallback model, or human review queue.

pairs.label: Impute
pairs.detail: Fill a versioned value and optionally add a missingness indicator.
pairs.explanation: Fill a versioned value and optionally add a missingness indicator. The fill policy becomes part of the deployed model and can move the decision boundary.

pairs.label: Marginalize
pairs.detail: Integrate or sum over the missing variable under a learned probability model.
pairs.explanation: Integrate or sum over the missing variable under a learned probability model. Confidence should reflect that less evidence arrived.

pairs.label: Boundary shift
pairs.detail: A direct predictor can fail when production inputs or label relationships move away from training.
pairs.explanation: A direct predictor can fail when production inputs or label relationships move away from training. Monitor calibration and performance by time, source, and important user slice.

pairs.label: Assumption failure
pairs.detail: Likelihoods can be badly calibrated when the chosen distribution or independence structure is wrong.
pairs.explanation: Likelihoods can be badly calibrated when the chosen distribution or independence structure is wrong. Good-looking samples do not prove density quality or decision safety.

pairs.label: Unsafe authority
pairs.detail: A generated proposal must not silently become an external side effect.
pairs.explanation: A generated proposal must not silently become an external side effect. Validate format, policy, provenance, and authorization before execution or publication.

pairs.label: Memorization and leakage
pairs.detail: Generative outputs can reproduce sensitive or licensed training material.
pairs.explanation: Generative outputs can reproduce sensitive or licensed training material. Direct predictors can also leak membership or protected attributes through scores and explanations.
